notes: Classification note: the 12 included stars—HVS 1; HVS 2/US 708; HVS 3/HE 0437–5439; HVS 4; HVS 5; HVS 6; HVS 7; HVS 8; HVS 9; HVS 10; HVS 12; HVS 13—were selected because previous studies had already identified them as unbound HVSs, so they are recorded as follow_up rather than candidates_found (T:p2-b8). The paper retains these 12 as unbound in its final assessment (T:p10-b7). HVS 2 is still unbound although a Galactic-center origin is excluded (T:p10-b10); HVS 3 remains unbound although Milky Way and LMC origins are both consistent at 1σ (T:p10-b2). HVS 7's astrometric link is called suspect, but the paper does not remove it from the unbound sample (T:p7-b10). The four bound velocity outliers B 434, B 485, B 711, and B 733 are excluded: the paper explicitly calls them bound, and B 711/B 733 are disk runaways, not Galactic-unbound candidates (T:p2-b8; T:p9-b3). HD 271791 and HIP 60350 are only cited as prior context and are not part of this study (T:p1-b13).

HVS 1: Table 1 in T:p5-b0 and its image I:p5-b0 are cut off at the right after the μ_RA column; the μ_Dec value for HVS 1 is not present in the supplied material, so proper_motion_dec is omitted. No HVS 1-specific parallax, Galactocentric radius, Galactic-rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability is reported in the supplied material.

HVS 2: Target HVS 2 = US 708. Table 1 as transcribed truncates the proper motion columns after the μRA value; the μDec component (+2.28 ± 0.55 mas/yr) is taken from Section 5.1 (T:p8-b2). The paper lists two slightly different heliocentric distances for HVS 2: 19 ± 2.6 kpc (Table 1, derived here) and 18.5 ± 2.6 kpc (Section 5.1, from Hirsch et al. 2005); both are recorded. The Galactic rest-frame speed is quoted only approximately ("almost exactly 1,000 km/s"), with no error. No parallax, galactocentric radius, or bound/unbound probabilities are reported for this star (a Galactic center origin is said to be ruled out at >3σ, but no numeric probability value is given); the star's tangential motion is 673 ± 118 km/s, which is not one of the requested quantities.

HVS 3: T:p5-b0 Table 1 gives HVS 3 coordinates in sexagesimal J2000 notation; I retained RA in hourangle and Dec in deg. The Table 1 text transcription truncates the second proper-motion component, so the adopted μDec is taken from the explicit value at T:p10-b1. T:p10-b3 reports epoch-subset proper-motion fits without uncertainties, retained as distinct reported measurements. No individual parallax, galactocentric radius, Galactic-rest-frame total speed, or bound/unbound probability is numerically reported for HVS 3.

HVS 4: Table 1's final proper-motion column is truncated after HVS 4's RA component in both the text transcription and the supplied image (T:p5-b0, I:p5-b0), so no µDec value can be extracted. No numerical bound/unbound probability, Galactocentric radius, or Galactic-rest-frame speed is reported specifically for HVS 4.

HVS 5: The Table 1 row for HVS 5 is cut off at the right side in the supplied text and image (T:p5-b0, I:p5-b0): only the right-ascension proper-motion component is visible, so proper_motion_dec is omitted. No individual parallax, galactocentric radius, Galactic-rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability is reported for HVS 5.

HVS 6: For HVS 6, the supplied Table 1 row in T:p5-b0 and the table image I:p5-b0 are truncated after the μRA value; no numeric μDec is present in the supplied material, so proper_motion_dec is omitted. No individual parallax, galactocentric radius, Galactic-rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability is reported for HVS 6.

HVS 7: Table 1 reports the proper motion as a combined column (header 'μRA, μ ...'), but the supplied transcription (T:p5-b0) and table image (I:p5-b0) are truncated after the RA component for HVS 7, so the declination proper-motion component is not extractable from the supplied material. The text (T:p5-b2) states HVS 7 has the most uncertain proper motion measurement (total ±1.33 mas yr−1, based on 8 reference galaxies) and (T:p7-b10) that its trajectory is the only one counter-rotating, but gives no numerical component values. No individual galactocentric radius, Galactic-rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability is reported for HVS 7.

HVS 8: Table 1 (T:p5-b0 and I:p5-b0) lists two proper motion components (μRA, μDec), but in the supplied transcription and image the μDec column is cut off after the μRA value, so only μRA = -0.82 ± 1.16 mas/yr could be extracted for HVS 8; no μDec value is available in the supplied material. Table 1 gives positions in sexagesimal J2000 coordinates (RA in hours, Dec in degrees).

HVS 9: The supplied Table 1 is cut off after the μ_RA column; HVS 9's μ_Dec is not numerically reported in the supplied text or visible table image (T:p5-b0, I:p5-b0), so proper_motion_dec is omitted. Figure 3 (I:p6-b0) plots HVS 9's proper motion but does not provide exact numerical labels.

HVS 10: The Table 1 material at T:p5-b0 and I:p5-b0 is cropped after the μRA column, so the proper-motion declination component for HVS 10 is not explicitly reported in the supplied table; Figure 3 (I:p6-b0) shows it only graphically, so no numerical value is extracted. Coordinates are reported in sexagesimal J2000 notation.

HVS 12: The Table 1 transcription and the table image (I:p5-b0) are truncated at the right edge, so only the first proper-motion component (mu_RA) is legible for HVS 12; the declination proper motion is not unambiguously reported in the supplied material. Figure 3 (I:p6-b0) shows HVS 12's proper motion graphically but no numeric value is stated in the text for its Dec component. RA is given sexagesimally in hours and Dec in degrees.

HVS 13: The text transcription of Table 1 (T:p5-b0) truncates HVS 13's proper-motion entry after the RA component; the Dec proper-motion component was read from the table image I:p5-b0. The paper does not report an individual bound/unbound probability, galactocentric radius, or Galactic-rest-frame speed for HVS 13.
